changes.evidence: What If...? S1E1: Schmidt runs HYDRA as Hitler's division and answers to the Reich; Hitler sends General Roeder to summon him to Berlin. Schmidt says a god doesn't answer to a man, shoots Roeder and says the Third Reich will fall and HYDRA will rise ('Hail Hydra'). Nazi Germany is a past group he breaks with in the same episode (the main red-skull record has the same Nazi Germany stage).

What If...? S2E4 (episode 13): Valkyrie beats Topaz, melts the Grandmaster and is crowned king of Sakaar, so he is deposed (the main grandmaster record goes Sakaar to Independent at Thor: Ragnarok for the same overthrow). In the mid-credits scene he is a puddle begging Topaz to collect him.

What If...? S1E4: before the crash Strange is a neurosurgeon working with Christine (she praises his successful radical hemispherectomy). Metro-General Hospital appears in the episode, and the MCU wiki lists him as a former Metro-General employee (by-christine-palmer has Metro-General Hospital). He then leaves to train at Kamar-Taj. This is a past workplace, so it goes first.

Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S1E3 'The Asset': Coulson briefs that Hall, a S.H.I.E.L.D. asset, has been kidnapped. Fitz and Simmons remember him as their second-year chemical kinetics advisor, i.e. an instructor at the S.H.I.E.L.D. Academy (employment, not study).

changes.evidence: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S1E3 'The Asset': Hall himself arranged his 'kidnapping' by Ian Quinn to escape S.H.I.E.L.D. He plans to drop the gravitonium, killing the town, and tells Coulson S.H.I.E.L.D. is just as guilty. He turns on S.H.I.E.L.D. and belongs to no group afterwards (he only pretends to work with Quinn).
